title: Analytic number theory
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Gauss sums of primitive characters and the Pólya–Vinogradov bound
modules.note:
The Gauss sum of a primitive Dirichlet character mod `q` has absolute value `√q`. For a
non-principal character mod `q`, every partial sum of its values is at most `2 √q (1 + log q)` in
absolute value.

* `New.norm_gaussSum_of_isPrimitive`: the modulus of the Gauss sum.
* `New.polya_vinogradov`: the Pólya–Vinogradov inequality.
modules.literature:
Known result: the Pólya–Vinogradov inequality for sums of a non-principal Dirichlet character. It is
proved here for initial intervals only, with the explicit bound `2 √q (1 + log q)`. The case of a
general character is reduced to the primitive character that induces it by a Möbius sieve. Source:
Pólya 1918, Vinogradov 1918; Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory; Montgomery–Vaughan Thm 9.18.

modules.title: Theta series of Dirichlet characters, Poisson summation, and `L(s, χ)` as a Mellin transform
modules.note:
For a parity `j ∈ {0, 1}`, the weight `w(z) = z ^ j e^(-π z²)` and coefficients `c(n)`, this file
studies the theta series `θ(u) = u ^ (1/2) ∑_{n ≥ 1} c(n) w(n u)`. It bounds `θ` and expresses its
Mellin transform through the Dirichlet series of `c`. For a Dirichlet character `χ ≠ 1` of parity
`j`, Poisson summation bounds the series near `0` and so gives the formula for `L(s, χ)` in
`re s > 0` (`hasMellin_thetaSeries_char`); if `χ` is also primitive, it gives the transformation
formula of `|θ|` (`norm_thetaSeries_inv`).
modules.literature:
Known result: the transformation formula and the Mellin transform of the theta series of a Dirichlet
character. Sources: Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory; Montgomery–Vaughan, Multiplicative
Number Theory I, ch. 10. Form here: the transformation is proved in absolute value only, so no root
number appears.

modules.title: Quadratic twists, polar functions and logarithmic derivatives of Dirichlet L-functions
modules.note:
This part shows that the twist of a Dirichlet character by the Legendre symbol of an odd prime not
dividing the modulus is not principal. It defines `New.IsPolar`, the condition that a Laplace-type
transform of an error term continues meromorphically with at most simple poles in the right
half-plane. It also expresses `∑ χ(n) Λ(n) n^{-s}` through the logarithmic derivative of
`New.entireL χ` and identifies the residues of that logarithmic derivative with the orders of the
zeros of `New.entireL χ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.quadTwist_ne_one`: the twist of a character modulo `N` by the Legendre symbol `(·/d)`, for an
  odd prime `d` prime to `N`, is not principal.
* `New.IsPolar`: `E` is measurable, `|E v| ≤ C e^v` for `v ≥ 0`, and `∫₀^∞ E(v) e^{(1-s)v} dv`
  continues to a meromorphic function of `s` with at most simple poles of residue `r ρ` in
  `re ρ > 0`.
* `New.LSeriesHasSum_mul_vonMangoldt`: `∑ χ(n) Λ(n) n^{-s}` in terms of the logarithmic derivative
  of `New.entireL χ`.
* `New.tendsto_sub_mul_logDeriv_entireL_analyticOrderNatAt`: the residues of that logarithmic
  derivative are the orders of the zeros of `New.entireL χ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.entireL`: The entire function equal to L(s, χ) if χ is not principal, and to the continuation
  of (s − 1)L(s, χ) if χ is principal.

modules.title: Landau's lemma
modules.note:
This part proves Landau's lemma: the moment generating function of a measure is not analytic at
its abscissa of convergence. It applies the lemma to transforms satisfying `New.IsPolar`. Assume
a one-sided bound on the error term `E`, and assume that the residues `r x` at real `x > β` have
non-negative real part. Then the part concludes that there is no pole to the right of `β`.
Together with `Lib.Analytic.EntireLFunction`, these are the analytic tools for passing from a
one-sided bound on an error term to the absence of zeros of L-functions.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_Ioi_subset_integrableExpSet_of_analyticAt`: Landau's lemma; the Laplace transform of
  a measure is not analytic at its abscissa of convergence.
* `New.IsPolar.landau`: let `β > 0`. If `E v ≤ A e^{(β-1)v}` for all large `v` and `re (r x) ≥ 0`
  for real `x > β`, then `r ρ = 0` for `re ρ > β`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsPolar` (from `Lib.Analytic.EntireLFunction`): `E` is measurable, `|E v| ≤ C e^v` for
  `v ≥ 0`, and `∫₀^∞ E(v) e^{(1-s)v} dv` continues meromorphically with at most simple poles of
  residue `r ρ` in `re ρ > 0`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Landau's lemma on Dirichlet integrals of one sign. It is applied to transforms with
simple poles whose residues at real points have non-negative real part: no pole lies to the right
of the abscissa given by the one-sided bound. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative
Number Theory I, 2007, Lemma 15.1 (Widder, The Laplace Transform, 1941, II Thm 5b).

modules.title: A prime `d` in a class whose quadratic twists have no zero in a box
modules.note:
Fix a class modulo `N` whose primes are `≡ 7` modulo `8` and prime to `N`, and a box
`re s ≥ β = 1/2 + 9 δ`, `|im s| ≤ H`. A prime `d` of the class is bad (`IsBadPrime`) if some
`L(s, ξ (·/d))`, with `ξ` modulo `N`, has a zero in the box. The main estimate is the count
`zero_density_quadTwist`: there are `O(X ^ (1 - δ / 2))` bad primes up to `X`. Such a count also
follows from the large sieve inequality for real characters; the proof here needs only the
Pólya–Vinogradov inequality, because theta series keep all sums short.

1. For a primitive character `χ ≠ 1` of conductor `q ≤ T²` let `J(χ, T)` be the integral over
   `u ≥ 1 / T` of `|θ_χ(u)| + |θ_{μχ}(u)|` against `du / u` (`thetaTailIntegral`). If `χ` has parity
   `j`, the Mellin transform of `θ_χ` at `s - 1/2` is `Γ_j L`, and by the functional equation the
   integral of `|θ_χ(u)| du / u` over `u < q ^ (-1/2)` equals that over `u > q ^ (-1/2)`. The
   truncated transform `𝓜` of `θ_{μχ}` (`mollifier`) approximates `Γ_j / L` on `re s = 2`.
2. For large `T` a zero in the box forces `J(χ, T) > T ^ (2 δ)`
   (`eventually_rpow_lt_thetaTailIntegral`). Otherwise `Γ_j L 𝓜 - Γ_j²` is `≪ T ^ (4 δ)` on
   `re s = 1/2` and `≪ 1 / T` on `re s = 2`, so it is small at the zero by the three-lines theorem,
   while it equals `-Γ_j²` there.
3. In the mean over `v ≤ T²` the theta series with coefficients `αₙ (-v/n°)`, where `n°` is the odd
   part of `n`, are small (`sum_sq_thetaSeries_jacobiSym_le`): expand the square, bound the pairs
   with `(n n')°` a square trivially and the others by Pólya–Vinogradov. So the sum of the `J` is
   `≪ T ^ (2 + δ)`.
4. By reciprocity `(n/d) = (-d/n°)`, so 2 and 3 give the count, with `T² = N X`, after passing from
   `ξ` to the primitive character that induces it.
5. If all primes of an invertible class were bad, the sum of `log p / p` over the class would
   converge; it diverges, so some prime of the class is not bad
   (`exists_entireL_quadTwist_ne_zero`).

Notions from other files:
* `gaussianMonomial j` is the weight `w(z) = z ^ j e^(-π z²)` of parity `j`, and `gaussianMellin j`
  is its Mellin transform `Γ_j(s) = ∫_0^∞ w(z) z ^ s dz / z`.
* `thetaSeries j c u` is `θ_c(u) = u ^ (1/2) ∑_{n ≥ 1} c(n) w(n u)`.
* `quadTwist χ d` is the character `χ (·/d)` modulo `N d`, for `χ` modulo `N` and a prime `d`.
modules.literature:
Known result: zero density for quadratic twists by mean values over real characters. Sources:
Jutila, On mean values of Dirichlet polynomials with real characters, Acta Arith. 27 (1975);
Heath-Brown, A mean value estimate for real character sums, Acta Arith. 72 (1995). Form here: a weak
density bound for the twists of the characters of a fixed modulus, by a smoothed mean square of
Jacobi symbol sums.

modules.title: Primes congruent to `1` modulo `M ^ k` with logarithm in a prescribed window
modules.note:
Let `4 ∣ M` and let `A` be fixed. For large `W` there is a prime `p ≡ 1` modulo `M ^ k` with `log p`
in `[U, U + W]`, uniformly for `1 < k`, `M ^ k ≤ W ^ A` and `W ≤ U ≤ W ^ A`
(`New.exists_prime_modEq_one_log_mem`).

The characters modulo `M ^ k` with trivial square come from the fixed modulus `M ^ 2`, so the
zero-free region gives a disc about `1` without zeros, uniformly in `k`. Newman's contour argument
on its boundary yields the prime.

Independently, the first section proves `n ≤ φ n * (2 * log n + 1)` (`New.le_totient_mul_log`).

Notions from other files:
* `entireL χ` is `L(s, χ)`, times `s - 1` if `χ` is principal;
* `regularL χ` is `L(s, χ)`, times `(s - 1) / s` if `χ` is principal.
modules.literature:
Known result: primes congruent to `1` modulo `M ^ k` with logarithm in a prescribed window. It is a
consequence of the Siegel–Walfisz theorem. Only one prime is found, in a long window, and only for
moduli that are powers of a fixed multiple of `4`. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative
Number Theory I, 2007, Cor. 11.19.

modules.title: Growth of Dirichlet L-functions near the line `re s = 1`
modules.group: The prime number theorem in progressions
modules.note:
Let `χ` be a character modulo `N`, and let `𝖿_χ(s)` (`regularL χ s`) be `L(s, χ)`, times
`(s - 1) / s` if `χ` is principal. Partial summation gives `|𝖿_χ(s)| ≤ 1 + 4 N |s|` in
`re s ≥ 1 / 2`, and the three-lines theorem improves this to `|𝖿_χ(s)| ≤ l²` for `re s ≥ 1 - 1 / l`
and `|s| ≤ 3 e^l`, whenever `l ≥ 10¹⁰` and `N ≤ e^l`.

Notions from other files:
* `entireL χ`: the entire function equal to `L(s, χ)` if `χ` is not principal, and to the
  continuation of `(s - 1) L(s, χ)` if it is.
modules.literature:
Known result: the bound `L(s, χ) ≪ log (N |s|)` near `re s = 1` and away from the pole. It is proved
here for `𝖿_χ` and with a square in place of the first power. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan,
Multiplicative Number Theory I, 2007, Lemma 10.15.

modules.title: A Tauberian theorem with a power of the logarithm
modules.group: The prime number theorem in progressions
modules.note:
Let `R` be measurable and Lipschitz on `v ≥ 0`, and let its transform `∫₀^∞ R(v) e^{(1 - s) v} dv`
be `(F s - F 1) / (s - 1)` in `re s > 2`. Suppose that for all large `l` the function `F` is
holomorphic and at most `l ^ A` on `re s ≥ 1 - l ^ (-A)`, `|s| ≤ e ^ l`. Then `R(v) = O(v ^ (-B))`
for every `B`. The theorem is meant for the remainder in the prime number theorem for a sum over
prime powers with weights that vanish at the cutoff `x`: at `x = e ^ v` it is Lipschitz in `v`.

The proof reads one Taylor coefficient of the transform at a far point `1 + H` in two ways. It is a
mean of `R` against a Gamma density that is concentrated at the given point `u`, hence close to
`R(u)`; and it is small by Cauchy's estimate on a disc that reaches left of the line `re s = 1`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the passage from a zero-free region to the error term of the prime number theorem.
Source: Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I, 2007, Section 6.2, where a contour
integral is used in place of the Taylor coefficient.

modules.title: A zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions
modules.group: The prime number theorem in progressions
modules.note:
For a Dirichlet character `χ` and large `l`, the function `L(s, χ)` has no zero with
`re s ≥ 1 - l⁻²⁵` and `|s| ≤ e^l`, and its logarithmic derivative, with the pole removed, is at most
`2 l²⁵` there. The inequality `|L(σ, 1)³ L(σ + i t, χ)⁴ L(σ + 2 i t, χ²)| ≥ 1` bounds `L` from below
to the right of `re s = 1`, and the bound for the derivative carries this across the line. If `χ²`
is principal, the points near `1` are treated by `𝖿_χ(1) ≠ 0` and continuity; so how large `l` must
be depends on `χ`.

Notions from other files:
* `entireL χ`: the entire function `L(s, χ)`, or `(s - 1) L(s, χ)` if `χ` is principal;
* `regularL χ`, written `𝖿_χ` in comments: `entireL χ`, divided by `s` if `χ` is principal.
modules.literature:
Known result: the classical zero-free region, in the crude form with a power of the logarithm that
the 3-4-1 inequality gives directly. Source: Montgomery and Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I,
2007, ch. 11.
